description: Erreygers/Wagstaff-style concentration indices (rineq::ci(), type='CIw') quantifying how each indicator is distributed across the DHS continuous wealth score (v191). Negative = outcome concentrated among the poor; positive = concentrated among the wealthy. This is a different, complementary method to a discrete 5-quintile breakdown (task2_wealth_quintile.csv) -- it answers the same 'does this vary by wealth' question using the full wealth continuum rather than 5 bins.

provenance.extracted_by: reading the rendered PDF's concentration-curve figures directly (Figures 4, 7, 10) -- the underlying .qmd's inline prose stats did not evaluate due to a missing `r` engine prefix, but the code-chunk-generated plots, including their annotated values, rendered correctly
provenance.note: The source commit's git tree is not reachable via a normal `git checkout` of task2-regional-indicators -- the file exists as a git blob but the branch tip's recorded tree does not include it (likely a broken commit from a GUI tool). Recovered via `git cat-file -p <blob-sha>`. See PLAN.md for the exact blob hashes and recovery command.
provenance.sample_note: Computed on a 12-35 month age band (harmonized across all three indicators), not the 6-59 month band used for this repo's committed national/county stunting figures (17.4%) -- see PLAN.md for the resulting methodological discrepancy that needs team reconciliation before this is treated as final.

indicators.interpretation: Stunting is concentrated among poorer children -- a poorer child is meaningfully more likely to be stunted than a wealthier one.
Incomplete vaccination is concentrated among poorer children -- a smaller gap than stunting's, but the same direction.
Skilled birth attendance is heavily concentrated among wealthier households -- the largest wealth gap of the three indicators, and the strongest single equity finding in this analysis so far.
